Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
235 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Minor tweaks to temperatures and cloud cover today through Wednesday 
as benign weather continues. Update timing and PoPs late week as a 
series of upper level troughs pass through. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Above normal temperatures and dry conditions through
  Wednesday with increasing rain chances Thursday into early
  next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Above normal temperatures and dry conditions through 
Wednesday with increasing rain chances Thursday into early next
week.

It's another dry day ahead with passing high level clouds from time 
to time as upper level ridging remains entrenched over the region. 
Surface high pressure will continue to meander offshore before 
shifting further out into the western Atlantic Wednesday. As a 
result, expect mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies for today and 
Wednesday with a steady supply of southerly return flow. 

Expect pockets of patchy fog this morning with temperatures starting 
out in the 40s. Highs will quickly warm into the 50s and 60s this 
morning with low to mid 70s this afternoon. Lows tonight will fall 
back into the upper 40s and low 50s with highs back in the low to 
mid 70s Wednesday. A few locations could punch into the upper 70s in 
the lee of Alleghenies and south/east of Washington DC Wednesday 
afternoon given increased southerly flow. 

Overall Wednesday will be our day of transition given the buckling 
ridge/departing high pressure offshore and incumbent upper level 
trough approaching from the Upper Midwest/Great Lakes region. This 
will lead to increasing clouds Wednesday afternoon with rain chances 
likely arriving from the west as early as Wednesday evening into 
Wednesday night. Current 18z/00z guidance suggests a weaker system 
for Thursday leading to lower rain amounts. This is largely due in 
part to the trough passing north and west of the region from the 
northern Ohio River Valley/eastern Great Lakes keeping the bulk of 
the forcing north of the region. The resultant surface front is set 
to cross sometime Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon leading 
to scattered showers and a few t-storms. Rainfall amounts Thursday 
will range between a tenth to a quarter of an inch with locally 
higher totals west of the Alleghenies where better forcing resides. 
Despite increased cloud cover expect highs back into the low to mid 
70s (60s mountains) Thursday afternoon. Storm total rain through 
Friday night will generally be between a quarter to a half an inch. 

A secondary upper level trough and associated cold frontal boundary 
will cross the region Friday into Saturday. Once again this system 
will be fairly progressive per the past few model cycles. This 
system looks to skip across the Alleghenies and Blue Ridge before 
redeveloping east of I-95. This is due largely in part to the upper 
level trough cutting off over the Great Lakes Friday evening into 
Saturday morning. At the surface, this will yield a dry slot ahead 
of the cold frontal boundary leading to higher rain chances over the 
mountains and in areas along/east of I-95. With that said, NBM PoPs 
continue to remain too high based upon this set up versus the 
deterministic/ensemble guidance. Weak high pressure will slide in 
from the southwest Saturday into Sunday cutting down rain chances 
over the weekend ahead. 

The high will be short-lived with another strong trough set to cross 
the area late Sunday into Monday. This system appears much larger 
than the previous two and more potent in delivering an airmass 
change for next week. Periods of showers are possible late Sunday 
night through early Tuesday morning although timing, coverage, and 
placement are yet to be determined. Upslope precip may linger 
Tuesday into Wednesday within northwest flow. Highs Monday and 
Tuesday will return back into the upper 50s and mid 60s (40s 
mountains). 

&&

.AVIATION /07Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions and light south/southeasterly winds at 
less than 15 kts will continue through Wednesday as high pressure 
meanders over the western Atlantic. Some patchy fog is possible at 
terminals along and east of I-95 this morning and again 
tonight/Wednesday morning given the uptick in moisture advection. 
This will lead to brief reductions in cigs/vsbys during the 9-13z/4-
8am time window. VFR conditions continue into Thursday although 
brief sub-VFR reductions are possible at times with showers and even 
a few thunderstorms Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon. South 
to southwesterly winds continue at less than 15 kts. 

Additional sub-VFR reductions are possible at times Friday into 
Friday night as a secondary trough of low pressure/front push 
through. VFR conditions will prevail overall although showers during 
the morning and afternoon/evening hours over the mountains and at 
terminals along/east of I-95 could lead to brief reductions. Winds 
will shift to the west Friday and eventually northwest Friday night 
into Saturday. VFR conditions return Saturday into Sunday with 
another round of sub-VFR conditions late Sunday night into Monday as 
a stronger trough pushes through. 

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through Wednesday morning. Winds will 
remain light out of the south and southeast through Wednesday as 
high pressure pushes offshore. By Wednesday evening into Thursday 
morning, expect the potential for southerly channeling due to the 
high offshore and incumbent trough from the northern Ohio River 
Valley. Confidence in this occurring is low with a focus over the 
middle and open waters. 

Low pressure and a strong cold front will work across the waters 
Thursday into Friday. Widespread showers and perhaps a few 
thunderstorms are possible Thursday afternoon. Winds will remain 
just below SCA levels both days with westerly gusts under 15 kts. 
Weak high pressure returns Saturday before another strong front 
crosses late Sunday into Monday. This front will bring a 
greater likelihood of SCA conditions across the waters heading 
into early next week.
